gaps.term: multiplier called only for ring products
gaps.quote: The multiplier is called only after
gaps.note: Overstated. The page says the established multiplier is called only after the Fourier transforms are reduced to polynomial products over C[y]/(y^r+1), via signed packing into four products on O(rp) bits. The paper also calls it elsewhere, for chirp numerators: squares and products of O(p)-bit numerators, computed with the established O(N log(2N)) multiplier at a cost of O(d p^{1+delta}) per entry (paper.tex lines 4891-4895), and for the small twist and scalar pointwise products on O(p)-bit numerators (lines 4896-4898). These are not ring-product calls. The paper's own summaries say only that polynomial products use signed packing and the multiplier (lines 202-204), and that calls to the multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls (lines 328-329). The correct statement is that the ring products go through signed packing, and other integer products on O(p)-bit numerators also use the multiplier.
